reason: The amendment-002 SSH procedure (phase17d_ssh_capture_v2.sh) produced an EMPTY capture: a 24-byte pcap (global header only), 0 packets, 0 SYN to dst port 22, while its metadata still printed ssh_attempts=60. The SSH traffic step opened zero TCP connections and the failure was hidden by output redirection and a static attempt-count echo.

attempt_002_failure_evidence.pcap_note: 24 bytes is exactly the pcap global header; no packet records were written

root_cause.summary: phase17d_ssh_capture_v2.sh generated no TCP traffic; each ssh/sshpass attempt aborted before opening a socket and the error was silenced.

responsible_lines_v2.L2: set -euo pipefail (with the trailing '|| true' on L36 this neutralises -e for the ssh step)
responsible_lines_v2.L19: tcpdump started with '>/dev/null 2>&1 &' so any startup error is invisible
responsible_lines_v2.L22: blind 'sleep 3' instead of a tcpdump-readiness check
responsible_lines_v2.L25_L36: sshpass/ssh attempt with forced legacy options (HostKeyAlgorithms=+ssh-dss, KexAlgorithms=+diffie-hellman-group1-sha1) that a modern OpenSSH client rejects at config-parse time (exit 255 before any TCP connect); the trailing '>/dev/null 2>&1 || true' hides the error and continues the loop
responsible_lines_v2.L52: echo "ssh_attempts=$ATTEMPTS" prints the static constant regardless of whether any connection was opened

root_cause.why_pcap_24_bytes: tcpdump started and wrote the 24-byte pcap global header, but zero packets matched 'host 192.168.50.20 and port 22' because no TCP connection to :22 was ever opened, so the file never grew beyond the header.
root_cause.why_metadata_claimed_60: the attempt count was a hard-coded echo of the ATTEMPTS constant (L52), never a count of connections actually opened.
root_cause.trigger_disambiguation: cannot be disambiguated without in-guest execution between (a) modern OpenSSH rejecting the forced legacy algorithm options and (b) sshpass being unavailable; both yield identical evidence. Amendment 003 removes dependence on ssh and sshpass entirely, so the exact trigger no longer matters.

replacement_procedure.connection_primitive: bash /dev/tcp/192.168.50.20/22 per attempt (guaranteed TCP SYN to the SSH port), sending an SSH-2.0 client identification banner and reading the server banner, then closing; independent of the ssh client and sshpass and of algorithm negotiation
orchestration_fixes: tcpdump started with stderr to a log and '-U' (packet-buffered writes)
readiness check: poll until tcpdump prints 'listening on' or the process dies, instead of a blind sleep; abort with exit 3 if not ready
per-attempt outcome logged to <run>.attempts.log; connections actually opened are counted (ssh_connections_opened), not a static constant
after capture: verify pcap grew beyond the 24-byte header or exit 4 (FAILURE pcap_header_only)
after extraction: verify the CSV has at least one data row or exit 5 (FAILURE csv_no_rows)
the success RESULT block is emitted only if both verifications pass

unchanged_and_reaffirmed.benign_and_portscan_runs: already ACCEPTED; not touched or re-acquired
unchanged_and_reaffirmed.acceptance_criteria: unchanged (a capture-integrity check for a non-empty pcap is an added guard, not a relaxation)
